traceability.evidence:
Implementation and tests directly matching Story 003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS are present and all tests pass.
1) Core rules and shared helpers - Rule implementations: - src/rules/require-story-annotation.ts - Uses shared helpers and visitors for function detection and scope: - Imports DEFAULT_SCOPE, EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES, shouldProcessNode from './helpers/require-story-helpers'. - In create(context): - const scope = opts.scope || DEFAULT_SCOPE; - const exportPriority = opts.exportPriority || 'all'; - const should = (node: any) => shouldProcessNode(node, scope, exportPriority); - Returns buildVisitors(context, sourceCode, { shouldProcessNode: should, scope, exportPriority }); - meta.schema defines the same configurable options documented in the story: - scope: array of node type strings (enum DEFAULT_SCOPE) - exportPriority: enum EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES - Error message is clear and actionable, including example story path: - messages.missingStory: "Function '{{name}}' must have an explicit @story annotation. Add a JSDoc or line comment with @story that points to the implementing story file (for example, docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md)."
- src/rules/require-req-annotation.ts - Shares the same scope and exportPriority semantics via require-story helpers: - Imports DEFAULT_SCOPE, EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES, shouldProcessNode from './helpers/require-story-helpers'. - In create(context): computes scope from options or DEFAULT_SCOPE and exportPriority from options or 'all', then uses shouldProcessNode(node, scope, exportPriority) for all function-like visitors. - Visitors enforce @req on the required function-like constructs: - FunctionDeclaration(node) { runCheck(node); } - FunctionExpression(node) { if parent is MethodDefinition, return; else runCheck(node); } - MethodDefinition(node) { runCheck(node); } - TSDeclareFunction(node) { runCheck(node); } - TSMethodSignature(node) { runCheck(node); } - Error message includes function-specific context and example fix: - messages.missingReq: "Function '{{functionName}}' is missing a required @req annotation. Add a JSDoc or line comment with @req (for example, '@req REQ-EXAMPLE') referencing the appropriate requirement from the story file."
- Shared detection & configuration logic: - src/rules/helpers/require-story-core.ts - DEFAULT_SCOPE: [ 'FunctionDeclaration', 'FunctionExpression', 'MethodDefinition', 'TSMethodSignature', 'TSDeclareFunction' ] -> Matches REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION node types; note ArrowFunctionExpression is not included here (excluded by default). - EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES: ['all', 'exported', 'non-exported'].
- src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts - Implements common scope/exportPriority behavior used by both rules via shouldProcessNode(node, scope, exportPriority): - Returns false if node.type not in scope. - Computes exported via isExportedNode(node), then applies exportPriority === 'exported'/'non-exported' rules. - Error location behavior: - reportMissing(...) computes name and nameNode (id/key identifiers or node itself) and calls context.report({ node: nameNode, messageId: 'missingStory', data: { name, functionName: name }, ... }). - reportMethod(...) similarly anchors the error at the method key identifier, satisfying REQ-ERROR-LOCATION. - Robust JSDoc/comment parsing for @story (REQ-JSDOC-PARSING & Error Handling): - jsdocHasStory: uses sourceCode.getJSDocComment(node) and checks jsdoc.value for '@story'. - commentsBeforeHasStory: uses sourceCode.getCommentsBefore(node) and scans for '@story'. - leadingCommentsHasStory, linesBeforeHasStory, parentChainHasStory, fallbackTextBeforeHasStory all used via hasStoryAnnotation, wrapped in try/catch to fail gracefully on malformed inputs.
- src/utils/annotation-checker.ts and src/utils/reqAnnotationDetection.ts - Provide the shared JSDoc/comment parsing strategy for @req used by require-req-annotation: - checkReqAnnotation(context, node, options?): - Uses context.getSourceCode(), getJSDocComment, leadingComments, getCommentsBefore, combineComments. - Calls hasReqAnnotation(jsdoc, all, context, node). - If !hasReq, calls reportMissing(context, node, enableFix). - hasReqAnnotation(...) combines multiple heuristics mirroring the @story rule: - linesBeforeHasReq(sourceCode, node) – scan preceding lines within LOOKBACK_LINES window. - parentChainHasReq(sourceCode, node) – walk parents and inspect comments/leadingComments. - fallbackTextBeforeHasReq(sourceCode, node) – scan preceding text window using FALLBACK_WINDOW. - Direct checks on jsdoc.value and comments for '@req' or '@supports'. - Guarded extensively with type checks and try/catch to avoid crashing on malformed JSDoc or AST, fulfilling Error Handling acceptance.
2) Function-like constructs & TypeScript support (REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION, REQ-TYPESCRIPT-SUPPORT) - For require-story-annotation, visitor construction: - src/rules/helpers/require-story-visitors.ts - buildFunctionDeclarationVisitor → FunctionDeclaration handler. - buildFunctionExpressionVisitor → FunctionExpression handler (skips MethodDefinition parents so MethodDefinition is handled separately). - buildMethodDefinitionVisitor → MethodDefinition handler. - buildTSDeclareFunctionVisitor → TSDeclareFunction handler. - buildTSMethodSignatureVisitor → TSMethodSignature handler. - buildArrowFunctionVisitor → ArrowFunctionExpression handler *behind* shouldProcessNode. - DEFAULT_SCOPE does NOT include 'ArrowFunctionExpression', so by default shouldProcessNode returns false for arrows: they are effectively excluded unless the user explicitly adds them to scope (matching "Arrow functions are excluded by default from traceability requirements").
- For require-req-annotation, visitors in src/rules/require-req-annotation.ts: - FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression (with MethodDefinition filter), MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature; no ArrowFunctionExpression visitor at all. - Combined with shared DEFAULT_SCOPE, this enforces the same function-like set across both rules.
- Tests verifying detection and TypeScript support: - tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts - Valid TS cases: - "[REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION] valid with annotation on TS declare function" (TSDeclareFunction) - "[REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION] valid with annotation on TS method signature" (TSMethodSignature) - Valid JS cases for FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, MethodDefinition. - Arrow function behavior: - Valid: "[REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED] unannotated arrow function allowed by default" – demonstrates that arrows are not enforced by default.
- tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts - Uses withTsLanguageOptions to exercise TS function expressions and exported TS function expressions. - Invokes runAnnotationCheckerTests from tests/utils/annotation-checker.test to validate TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature behavior: - Valid: TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature with @req. - Invalid: missing @req on both constructs, expecting missingReq errors with proper names.
3) Configurable scope and export priority (REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE, REQ-EXPORT-PRIORITY) - Implementation: - Both rules read an options object with 'scope' and 'exportPriority' and use DEFAULT_SCOPE/EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES. - shouldProcessNode in require-story-helpers.ts enforces: - Node type in allowed scope array. - exportPriority === 'all' | 'exported' | 'non-exported' with isExportedNode(...) consulting ExportNamedDeclaration/ExportDefaultDeclaration in parent chain.
- Tests for require-story-annotation (tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts): - "require-story-annotation with exportPriority option" block: - Valid: - Unexported function without @story is valid when { exportPriority: 'exported' }. - Exported function with annotation is valid. - Exported arrow function missing annotation is valid (arrows excluded). - Invalid: - Exported function missing @story with exportPriority: 'exported' triggers error and autofix. - "require-story-annotation with scope option" block: - Valid: arrow function with scope limited to ['FunctionDeclaration'] is ignored. - Invalid: FunctionDeclaration missing annotation is reported when in scope.
- Tests for require-req-annotation (tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts) extensively cover matching semantics: - Valid cases show nodes ignored or required according to scope/exportPriority. - Invalid cases explicitly assert behavior for: - exportPriority 'exported' vs 'non-exported' for functions, methods, and FunctionExpressions. - scope limited to ['FunctionDeclaration'] still reporting FunctionDeclaration.
4) Error location and user experience (REQ-ERROR-LOCATION, User Experience, Error Handling) - Error location: - require-story-annotation via reportMissing/reportMethod in require-story-helpers.ts uses the function identifier or method key as 'node' in context.report, ensuring precise error locations at the function name. - require-req-annotation via annotation-checker.reportMissing: - Determines name via getNodeName. - Picks nameNode as node.id or node.key identifier when available and uses it in context.report({ node: nameNode, ... }).
- User-facing messages: - Story rule: - messages.missingStory explains exactly what to add and cites a concrete example story path. - Suggestions generated by createAddStoryFix/respective helpers insert a minimal @story placeholder JSDoc. - Req rule: - messages.missingReq describes missing @req, includes functionName, and gives an example '@req REQ-EXAMPLE'.
- Robust error handling: - require-story-helpers.hasStoryAnnotation and reportMissing/reportMethod all wrap detection/reporting logic in try/catch to avoid crashing on malformed ASTs, missing APIs, or bad comments. - reqAnnotationDetection's advanced heuristics (linesBeforeHasReq, parentChainHasReq, fallbackTextBeforeHasReq) include: - Type guards on sourceCode, lines, range, and loc. - try/catch around sourceCode.getText() and range slicing. - Comments explicitly documenting that IO/detection failures are treated as "no annotation" instead of throwing.
5) Documentation (Acceptance Criteria: Documentation) - Rule docs are present and correctly reference this story and requirements: - docs/rules/require-story-annotation.md - @story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md - @req REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED - Require `@story` annotation on functions - Documents supported node types exactly matching REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION: - FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature. - Documents options (scope, exportPriority) with JSON schema and example config. - Provides JS and TS examples, including correct and incorrect cases.
- docs/rules/require-req-annotation.md - @story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md - @req REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED - Require `@req` annotation on functions - Describes supported node types mirroring require-story-annotation. - Explains defaults and semantics for 'scope' and 'exportPriority' matching the helper implementation. - Includes JS and TS examples for correct and incorrect uses.
6) Tests explicitly tied to Story 003.0 - tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts - Header: - "Tests for: docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md" - @story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md - @req REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED and REQ-REQUIRE-ACCEPTS-IMPLEMENTS. - Describe block name: "Require Story Annotation Rule (Story 003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS)". - Covers: - All function kinds (FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature). - Arrow functions allowed by default. - Auto-fix outputs and suggestions containing the correct story path. - exportPriority and scope behaviors.
- tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts - Header: - @story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md - @req REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED and REQ-TYPESCRIPT-SUPPORT. - Describe block name: "Require Req Annotation Rule (Story 003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS)". - Uses helper missingReq(...) to standardize error shapes. - Valid and invalid arrays exhaustively test: - FunctionDeclaration, FunctionExpression, MethodDefinition, TSDeclareFunction, TSMethodSignature. - Configurable scope and exportPriority semantics. - TypeScript-specific cases via withTsLanguageOptions and runAnnotationCheckerTests.
7) Test execution - Command executed (from earlier run): - npm test -- --runInBand --verbose - Underlying Jest invocation: jest --ci --bail --runInBand --verbose - All tests passed: - Test Suites: 35 passed, 35 total - Tests: 266 passed, 266 total - Output includes multiple suites directly referencing this story: - "Require Story Annotation Rule (Story 003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS)" with numerous [REQ-...] tests all passing. - "Require Req Annotation Rule (Story 003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS)" with REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION, REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE, REQ-EXPORT-PRIORITY, REQ-TYPESCRIPT-SUPPORT tests all passing. - Helper and edge-case test suites (Require Story Helpers, IO behavior, etc.) supporting robustness and error handling.
Taken together, this provides concrete evidence that: - Both require-story-annotation and require-req-annotation enforce their respective annotations on the same set of function-like constructs (with arrow functions excluded by default). - They share aligned scope/exportPriority semantics through common helpers. - They support JS and TS syntax including TSDeclareFunction and TSMethodSignature. - They implement robust JSDoc/comment parsing with graceful error handling. - Documentation is present and aligned with behavior. - Comprehensive, passing tests validate all key requirements from docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md.
traceability.notes: Story 003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS is fully implemented. The require-story-annotation and require-req-annotation rules share a common detection and configuration model via shared helpers, cover the specified function-like constructs (with arrow functions excluded by default), provide clear error messages anchored at the function name, support TypeScript constructs, and handle malformed comments defensively. Rule documentation exists and matches the implemented behavior. Multiple dedicated test suites for this story pass, including tests for function detection, TypeScript support, configurable scope, export priority, and error messaging, confirming that all acceptance criteria and technical requirements in the story are satisfied.
